content:
Lina Park: FYI - Cypress reported a short isolation for their on-prem inference agents at 03:40 UTC. Customers saw ~2min of 502s.
incident-bot: Alert: PEER_LINK_FLAP tenant=Cypress detected at 2026-11-17T03:40:12Z (auto-ticket INC-8899)
Ethan Moore: I replayed the netflow; looks like SNAT entries are being remapped during route churn. Behavior matches prior SNAT reassignment issue but on an older appliance.
Ravi Desai: Their edge box is still on v1.4.2 of the bootstrap image; conntrack default is tiny (nf_conntrack_max=65536). Might be hitting table churn.
Zoe Martinez: Can SE-Jordan confirm appliance model + conntrack tuning? SE-Jordan: Cypress confirms model CX-210, default conntrack untouched. They've only allowed maintenance windows Tuesdays.
Lina Park: Immediate triage: 1) ask customer to temporarily increase conntrack and SNAT sticky rule, 2) schedule a maintenance slot, 3) platform-side protective measure.
Ethan Moore: I can push a temporary sticky-SNAT snippet they can apply without reboot. Paste: ```
# temp sticky SNAT
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -m comment --comment "cypress-sticky" -j SNAT --to-source 198.51.100.45
```
Ravi Desai: We should also add a short debounce on route-programming in the peering controller; 20s might be enough and less likely to impact failover. I'll sketch an SR.
Zoe Martinez: Add feature flag, per-tenant. If Cypress wants immediate safety, we can flip flag for them after testing.
Lina Park: Owners & actions:
- Ethan: Send sticky-SNAT snippet + conntrack increase guidance to Cypress SE, add runbook note (JIRA: DED-4210) (ETA: 6h)
- Ravi: Design controller debounce + FF, branch peering/debounce-cypress (ETA: 4d)
- Zoe: Book maintenance window (Tue 2026-11-23 09:00 UTC) with Cypress, confirm appliance access (ETA: 2d)
- Lina: Add entry to recurring-incidents tracker and set up 30-day watch cadence (ETA: today)
Ethan Moore: DED-4210 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DED-4210 - includes snippet and quick rollback notes.
Ravi Desai: Quick log sample: ```
# netflow excerpt
src=10.77.1.9 dst=203.0.113.12 proto=tcp action=drop reason=SNAT_CHANGE
```
Zoe Martinez: Cypress requested a rollback procedure in case the debounce delays failover too much. Ravi - please include a CLI override and immediate revert steps in your PR.
Ravi Desai: Will do. PR will add metrics peering.debounce_duration and peering.debounce_blocked_routes so we can monitor side effects.
Lina Park: Also: add an infra CI job that simulates flapping peering and verifies session continuity. Ethan + Ravi pair on acceptance test. (ETA: 10d)
Ethan Moore: Noting recurrence: this is the fourth occurrence across customers in 8 months with similar SNAT churn signature. Recommend a small cross-team project to standardize on on-prem defaults.
Zoe Martinez: I'll draft an ops proposal for hardened defaults and propose it in next week's infra planning meeting.
incident-bot: Reminder scheduled: cypress-remediation-checkin every Mon 17:00 UTC for 4 weeks starting 2026-11-23
Lina Park: Summary: DED-4210 for customer config, branch + PR for controller debounce, CI test job, maintenance slot booked pending confirmation. Weekly check-ins for 30 days. Escalate to sprint if two recurrences in 90 days.
SE-Jordan: Cypress agreed to apply the temp SNAT today and will share conntrack sizing after maintenance.
Ethan Moore: I'll drop notes and the flow excerpts into DED-4210 and link to the recurring incidents page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/REC-PEER-002
Lina Park: Thanks everyone. If we see another flap before the maintenance, ping oncall and tag this thread. :raising_hand: 
Zoe Martinez: Closing loop - owners assigned and DED-4210 live. We'll reconvene at first check-in.
